title: Identity, Authorization & Revocation
purpose: Plan an evidence-backed study of caller identity, object ownership, authentication state and revocation so private AI-application data and actions remain bound to current authority.
productNeed: Users need private projects and sessions to stay private while intended sharing, administration and offboarding continue to work correctly.
securityObjective: Place authorization at authoritative API and data boundaries, distinguish ownership from roles and sharing, and make revoked authority stop taking effect across pending work.
scope: Trace one caller-to-object path, one authentication/session path and one revocation transition. Use source/design evidence first, then a bounded local relation fixture or native runtime only when the required execution scope is available.
dependencies: M01 threat-model foundation
HTTP/API and database authorization basics
Authentication/OAuth and session-state basics
Applicable local runtime, identities and written execution scope before native tests
boundaries: Caller identity → API/session boundary
API handler → authoritative object ownership or permission check
Current session/revocation state → pending or repeated operation
investigation: Trace caller, object and role arguments from request entry to the responsible control. Write expected owner, other-user, intended-share, admin and revoked-session outcomes before any permitted test.
control: Require current caller/object authorization at authoritative reads and writes; keep sharing/admin logic explicit; re-check revocation where delayed work or stale state can outlive an earlier decision.
permittedCases: Owner accesses the intended private object
Explicitly permitted share or admin path behaves according to its declared policy
deniedCases: Unrelated user reads or changes a private object
Revoked or stale identity continues a protected operation
evidencePlan: Pinned source trace and caller/object/action matrix
Dated allowed/denied predictions
Raw bounded request or fixture receipts only when executed
Revocation timeline, remediation/retest record and reviewer decision when available
evaluationCriteria: Legitimate owner and intended-share behavior remains available
Unrelated-user and revoked-state cases deny without unauthorized state change
Runtime claims require source/build/configuration parity and raw evidence
remediationRetest: Propose or review the authoritative check, then retest both the denied path and legitimate access. Add minimal actor/object/action decision telemetry and transfer the same invariant to a second route or product.
recoveryTransfer: Contain the affected route or grant, restore the approved authorization state after retest, preserve evidence, and repeat the principle on an unfamiliar authorization representation.
limitations: No native security result, confirmed vulnerability or reviewer acceptance is claimed.
Source/design work cannot by itself prove deployed runtime behavior.
Ownership, sharing, administration and tenancy remain separate policy questions.

title: Secure RAG & Data Lifecycle
purpose: Plan a case study covering trustworthy ingestion, permission-aware retrieval, memory boundaries and deletion across source data and derived copies.
productNeed: A knowledge assistant should ingest changing documents, retrieve only currently authorized content, preserve provenance and remove or restore data according to a documented lifecycle.
securityObjective: Keep permissions and provenance intact across upload, ingestion, indexing, retrieval, memory, caches and deletion instead of treating RAG as one undifferentiated step.
scope: Trace one upload/ingestion path, one permission-aware retrieval path and one lifecycle transition. A synthetic retriever or fixture may support mechanism learning; native ACL claims remain gated by the actual edition, configuration and runtime.
dependencies: M03 upload and parser boundary understanding
M05 data-flow analysis
RAG ingestion, indexing and retrieval fundamentals
Native Standard/permission prerequisites where the selected product path requires them
boundaries: Source document → ingestion/provenance metadata
Current user/group authority → retrieval filter → selected context
Stored source/memory → index/cache/backup copies → deletion or restoration
investigation: Map each copy and permission transition, predict permitted and denied retrieval, introduce only synthetic provenance changes, and trace how revocation, memory state or deletion should alter later context.
control: Validate ownership and provenance at ingestion, apply current authorization at retrieval, keep memory consent/provenance explicit and maintain a data-copy ledger with deletion/recovery criteria.
permittedCases: Authorized user retrieves an eligible document with expected provenance
Approved data survives a legitimate update or restore according to the declared policy
deniedCases: Unauthorized or stale-permission document appears in retrieved context
Deleted or disallowed content remains available from an unaccounted derived copy
evidencePlan: Ingestion provenance ledger and data-copy map
Retrieval authorization matrix and selected-context receipts when run
Memory consent/provenance record and deletion/restore criteria
Explicit native-versus-fixture attribution for every observation
evaluationCriteria: Allowed retrieval stays useful and provenance remains traceable
Denied or revoked content does not appear in the observed context under the declared scope
Deletion/recovery checks enumerate indexes, caches, memory and backup assumptions rather than hiding gaps
remediationRetest: Move permission checks to current authoritative state, quarantine or reprocess suspect ingestion, reconcile stale derived copies and rerun both permitted retrieval and denied/deleted cases.
recoveryTransfer: Document reindex/reconciliation steps, ownership of restored copies and revalidation triggers; transfer the invariant to a second retriever or data architecture without assuming identical ACL semantics.
limitations: Native connected-document ACL behavior is not claimed without the required product entitlement and runtime evidence.
A local fixture demonstrates only its own authorization and lifecycle behavior.
No production data, real connector account or external provider is included.

title: MCP & Agent Action Security
purpose: Plan a bounded agent-security study that binds identity, consent, delegated task, tool arguments and the actual side effect instead of treating model intent as authority.
productNeed: Tool-using agents need to call local MCP or action services without turning retrieved or tool-supplied text into permission, leaking credentials or duplicating effects after failure.
securityObjective: Constrain outbound identity and destinations, approve exact actions, re-check current authority at the effect service, and make retries, cancellation and peer delegation observable and recoverable.
scope: Study one MCP/action flow and one local effect type, then add a small peer/delegation fixture for M34. Prompt-injection evaluation is measured at the effect/data boundary, not by suspicious wording alone.
dependencies: M04/M06 configuration, secrets and identity foundations
M11 MCP/OAuth concepts before action or peer claims
M13 action-authorization contract before prompt-injection effect tests
Applicable local transport and authorization scope
boundaries: User → selected MCP/action credential and destination
Proposal → exact approval → current effect-service authorization
Peer task/delegation → stop/replay/reconciliation state
investigation: Trace credential selection, audience/destination, task and argument binding. Run or design legitimate, changed-argument, expired, replay, response-loss and hostile-input cases against a synthetic effect ledger.
control: Use task-scoped identity and consent, destination policy, exact approval records, current effect authorization, idempotency keys, stop/cancel semantics and authoritative effect receipts.
permittedCases: Authorized task with exact approved arguments creates the intended synthetic effect once
Legitimate retry reconciles a previously completed effect without duplication
deniedCases: Changed arguments, wrong caller/task, expired approval or unapproved destination reaches the effect
Hostile retrieved/tool text causes a forbidden action or peer delegation
evidencePlan: Outbound/inbound identity and consent matrix
Tool-policy contract and exact approval records
Synthetic effect receipts for allowed, denied, retry and stop cases
Prompt-injection corpus with outcome measured from authoritative state
evaluationCriteria: Security outcome is determined by actual effect/data state rather than model claims
Legitimate actions remain usable while wrong task/caller/arguments deny
Response loss, replay and cancellation produce explainable, reconcilable state
remediationRetest: Tighten the authoritative task/argument/destination check or retry contract, then rerun legitimate, denied and fault cases while validating the actual effect ledger.
recoveryTransfer: Stop the local effect path, reconcile uncertain completion, rotate only synthetic credentials if needed, and transfer the same task/effect invariant to a second action or peer surface.
limitations: No real external MCP server, SaaS account, payment, message or provider attack is included.
General native multi-agent capability is not assumed; added peers remain explicitly fixture/extension work.
Model behavior claims require an actual declared model and separate evaluation manifest.

title: Sandbox & Supply Chain Controls
purpose: Plan one deliberately narrow study: one executor boundary plus one related artifact-integrity or analysis gate, with native runtime prerequisites kept explicit.
productNeed: An AI application that executes code or produces artifacts needs a clearly bounded executor and a trustworthy way to decide which related image, dependency or artifact is allowed to run or ship.
securityObjective: Verify a single isolation boundary and a single artifact/provenance decision without implying a complete sandbox, host, supply-chain or platform audit.
scope: One executor boundary only (for example filesystem/network/process capability) and one related artifact question (for example image/dependency digest, provenance or a narrow analyzer rule). No second executor or broad platform review is included.
dependencies: Resolved executor backend/image and exact runtime identity
Known host/kernel/container capabilities and effective network/filesystem policy
Pinned artifact/dependency identity and declared trust root
Applicable authorization and resources for any native isolation test
boundaries: AI/application request → selected executor capability boundary
Pinned artifact or dependency → verification/analyzer gate → promotion/update decision
investigation: Review the executor contract and choose one benign isolation case plus one denied capability case. Separately verify one artifact identity/provenance or narrow analysis rule with known-good and known-bad synthetic inputs.
control: Apply one explicit executor restriction at the responsible boundary and one protected artifact or analyzer gate. Record trust roots, expected false positives/negatives and the update condition that triggers revalidation.
permittedCases: Benign executor task uses only the declared capability
Approved artifact or safe analyzer case passes the declared gate
deniedCases: Executor reaches the one explicitly forbidden capability
Mismatched, untrusted or known-bad artifact/analysis case is promoted
evidencePlan: Executor capability map for the selected boundary
Pinned runtime/artifact identities and effective configuration
Known-good/known-bad gate cases with false-positive/negative accounting
Update regression and rollback record if native prerequisites are later satisfied
evaluationCriteria: The selected legitimate executor workflow remains functional
The selected denied capability is blocked by the responsible boundary when actually tested
Artifact/analyzer decisions remain reproducible across an approved update or are marked for revalidation
remediationRetest: Change only the selected executor policy or artifact gate, review the diff, rerun the legitimate and denied case, then repeat after one controlled update input.
recoveryTransfer: Return to the authorized safe executor/artifact state, reconcile generated artifacts, preserve the failed/update evidence and transfer the narrow rule to one comparable runtime or artifact surface.
limitations: Native executor/runtime prerequisites are unresolved; no isolation claim is made until the exact backend, image, host/kernel capabilities and effective policy are verified.
Client code or Compose entries do not prove the external sandbox implementation.
This slot intentionally does not claim a comprehensive sandbox, supply-chain or vulnerability assessment.

title: Security Evaluation & Incident Operations
purpose: Plan a repeatable security-evaluation and incident-operations study around one synthetic usage or agent-action failure sequence.
productNeed: Teams changing prompts, tools or models need known-outcome regression checks, useful telemetry, accurate detections and a recovery process that can distinguish attempted, completed and uncertain effects.
securityObjective: Validate the evaluator and detector against authoritative state, keep invalid cases visible, and connect failures to containment, reconciliation, retest and reproducible handover.
scope: One synthetic usage/action scenario with a bounded known-outcome corpus, one event schema/detector, one fault/retry sequence and one handover. It is not a claim of complete red teaming or production incident coverage.
dependencies: M13/M15 action and hostile-input boundary as applicable
M24 evaluation contract and known outcomes
M25 event schema before incident conclusions
Declared synthetic effect ledger or other authoritative oracle
boundaries: Scenario → evaluator/adjudication → release decision
Authoritative effect/data state → telemetry → detection
Failure/alert → containment → reconciliation → handover
investigation: Seed legitimate, blocked, completed, duplicated, missing-event and malformed/timeout cases. Compare evaluator and detector output with independently known effect state and preserve invalid/uncertain outcomes.
control: Use authoritative state as the security oracle, version evaluation inputs and rules, minimize events, correlate request/task/effect IDs and require explicit containment/recovery owners.
permittedCases: Legitimate authorized task succeeds and is scored separately from security outcome
Known safe event sequence remains below the declared detector threshold
deniedCases: Forbidden effect is missed because model text claims refusal or success
Missing/malformed evidence is silently converted into a pass
evidencePlan: Versioned known-outcome corpus and evaluator manifest
Raw TP/FP/FN/TN or explicit non-binary outcome counts where applicable
Event/alert map, blind-spot register and synthetic incident timeline
Containment, restore/reconciliation, retest and handover packet
evaluationCriteria: Ground truth comes from the responsible service/store rather than assessed model text
Invalid, timeout and unsupported cases remain visible in denominators and release decisions
Another person can reproduce the stated outcome and limitations from the handover
remediationRetest: Repair the evaluator, detector, event mapping or retry logic that produced the mismatch; rerun known-good and known-bad controls before using the result for a release or incident decision.
recoveryTransfer: Contain the selected synthetic failure, reconcile actual effects, restore the authorized safe state and replay the same evaluation/operations pattern on a second product surface.
limitations: No production incident, customer impact, longitudinal telemetry or professional incident-command experience is claimed.
One bounded corpus cannot establish complete attack coverage or evaluator reliability.
Release thresholds and accountable owners remain hypothetical until an actual authorized context supplies them.

title: Model Robustness, Training & Privacy
purpose: Plan an optional model-security specialty using a real tiny model and synthetic data so robustness, training integrity and model-privacy claims have known ground truth.
productNeed: When a role owns model-level risk, the team needs valid experiments for evasion, poisoning/training lineage and privacy or extraction behavior—not proxy claims based only on application prompts.
securityObjective: Define valid perturbations, splits, attacker access and observable outputs before measuring robustness, training/artifact trust or privacy tradeoffs on a pinned small model.
scope: One real tiny supervised model or trainer with synthetic data, held-out evaluation and one bounded experiment per selected responsibility. Foundation-model fine-tuning, large weights and production serving are out of scope.
dependencies: ML/statistics foundations and M24 evaluation discipline
Pinned model/trainer, feature and label contract
Dataset/split provenance before training claims
Known synthetic membership/output ground truth before privacy claims
boundaries: Input/feature contract → model decision and clean/robust utility
Dataset/job identity → trained artifact → promotion
Observable model output → held-out privacy/extraction assessment
investigation: Pre-register valid and invalid perturbations, poisoning or membership cohorts, held-out data and utility metrics. Run only on declared synthetic data and preserve model/data/version identity.
control: Use constrained preprocessing, dataset/job/artifact lineage, promotion gates and privacy/output controls that can be retested against held-out data without leaking final labels into tuning.
permittedCases: Clean and valid perturbed inputs are evaluated under the same declared feature contract
Approved dataset/job/artifact lineage produces the expected promoted tiny model
deniedCases: Invalid perturbation or contaminated evaluation split is reported as security evidence
Unknown or unapproved training artifact is promoted or privacy conclusions are drawn without known membership ground truth
evidencePlan: Model, data, split and trainer manifest
Held-out outcome counts and utility comparison
Training/artifact lineage and promotion/recovery record
Explicit limitations tying every result to the tiny model and synthetic data used
evaluationCriteria: Attack and legitimate cohorts are valid under a fixed feature/output contract
Metrics report numerator/denominator and invalid cases rather than a single readiness score
Mitigation is judged alongside clean utility and transferred only with new evidence
remediationRetest: Adjust the selected preprocessing, training/promotion or output control; rerun held-out clean and attack/privacy cohorts and preserve the changed artifact identity.
recoveryTransfer: Roll back to the approved tiny-model artifact or dataset lineage, then repeat the mechanism on a second small model or feature schema without reusing unsupported conclusions.
limitations: This is an optional specialty for roles with model-level responsibility.
No native Onyx training, foundation-model security or production model assurance is claimed.
Results from one tiny synthetic model cannot be generalized to unrelated models or real user data.

title: AI Privacy, Policy & Product Assurance
purpose: Plan a product-assurance study that connects data minimization, safe output/reliance, lifecycle controls, supplier evidence and acceptable-use policy without inventing legal conclusions.
productNeed: An AI product needs clear rules for what data can reach providers/tools/logs, how answers and downloads are presented, how data is deleted, and what supplier or misuse evidence supports product decisions.
securityObjective: Make data, reliance and policy decisions traceable to concrete sinks, sources, lifecycle copies and independently reviewable evidence while preserving legitimate product use.
scope: Trace one provider/tool/log data boundary, one output/reliance path, one deletion/lifecycle decision and one supplier or acceptable-use decision using synthetic content and source/design evidence.
dependencies: M01/M05 data-flow and product-boundary foundations
Known provider/tool/log destination and data fields
Declared lifecycle copies and deletion assumptions
Actual supplier/service evidence and accountable specialists before real legal/procurement decisions
boundaries: User/retrieved data → provider/tool/log sink
Source/evidence → answer/link/download → human reliance
Data copies/supplier obligations/policy → product decision and exit or appeal path
investigation: Build field-to-sink, claim-to-source and copy-to-lifecycle matrices. Use harmless policy cases and supplier evidence to test whether a product decision is supported, unsupported or blocked by missing facts.
control: Minimize data before outbound boundaries, preserve safe rendering and provenance, define deletion/recovery criteria, record supplier responsibilities and evaluate policy controls with legitimate near-neighbor cases.
permittedCases: Approved data reaches an allowed sink and the user receives appropriately sourced output
Legitimate policy-compliant task remains usable under the declared privacy and reliance controls
deniedCases: Designated private synthetic canary reaches a denied sink or persists in an unaccounted copy
Unsupported supplier or policy evidence is presented as a legal, compliance or product-safety conclusion
evidencePlan: Data/sink register and minimized payload comparison
Claim/source or download-access matrix
Data-copy/deletion ledger and supplier responsibility matrix
Harmless policy corpus with false-refusal and unresolved-case accounting
evaluationCriteria: Denied synthetic fields stay out of declared sinks while allowed product behavior remains useful
Claims and product decisions distinguish observed evidence, source/design inference and unresolved questions
Policy evaluation includes safe near-neighbors so excessive refusal is visible
remediationRetest: Move minimization or output checks to the authoritative boundary, update lifecycle/supplier obligations or policy rules, then rerun both protected and legitimate cases with the changed evidence set.
recoveryTransfer: Reconcile persisted copies, revoke only synthetic credentials if required, document incident/exit or appeal ownership and transfer the evidence method to a second provider, policy or product surface.
limitations: No legal, compliance or procurement advice is claimed; real decisions require the relevant accountable specialists.
No real personal data, provider account or supplier contract is included.
A bounded policy corpus does not prove comprehensive misuse prevention or model safety.

title: Integrated AI Security Capstone
purpose: Plan the catalog’s synthetic support-summary action as an integrated case study covering authorized retrieval, exact action approval, telemetry, release gates, recovery and handover.
productNeed: A synthetic employee should be able to summarize only documents they may access and create one local support ticket through an independently authorized action service.
securityObjective: Carry one feature from design through authorized retrieval, constrained proposal, exact approval, effect verification, telemetry/evaluation, release change and safe recovery without granting authority to retrieved text or model output.
scope: Synthetic subject/workspace/document/task IDs, an authorized retrieval adapter, deterministic or mock summary generation, one local ticket effect, exact approval, minimized events, a known-outcome evaluator, one update and one rollback/reconciliation exercise. Use a standalone fixture if native prerequisites remain unresolved.
dependencies: M01/M02/M05 identity, object and data-flow foundations
M09 current retrieval authorization
M13 exact action approval and effect-service authority
M21/M24/M25/M27/M29 delivery, evaluation, telemetry, retry and update/recovery foundations
boundaries: Synthetic caller → authenticated entry service
Entry service → current authorized retrieval → selected context
Context → constrained summary/action proposal
Proposal → exact approval → local support-ticket effect service
Effect state → minimized telemetry/evaluator → release decision
Changed policy/schema/build → targeted regression → rollback/reconciliation
investigation: Pre-register allowed, denied and uncertain outcomes; verify current retrieval authority; bind approval to subject/task/tool/arguments/expiry; compare telemetry and evaluator output with the actual ticket ledger; then change one release input and exercise recovery.
control: Retrieved text remains data, not authority. The effect service re-checks current caller/task permission and exact arguments, writes idempotent receipts, supports stop/reconciliation, and emits minimized authoritative events for independently validated evaluation.
permittedCases: Authorized employee summarizes eligible documents and creates exactly one approved synthetic ticket
Approved update preserves the intended authorized flow
deniedCases: Wrong owner/workspace, stale permission or forbidden context reaches the summary
Changed arguments, wrong task/caller, expired approval or retry ambiguity creates an unauthorized or duplicate ticket
evidencePlan: Integrated threat/control map and pinned source/runtime manifest
Planned 24-case design with raw receipts and invalid counts added only after execution
Ticket-ledger, telemetry and evaluator correlation
Reviewed remediation/no-change rationale, update regression, rollback/reconciliation and independent handover
evaluationCriteria: Current retrieval permission determines context selection
Exact approval and current effect-service authority determine the ticket effect
Known-outcome evaluation uses authoritative state and keeps missing/malformed evidence INVALID or unresolved
Release change preserves legitimate behavior and recovery returns to an authorized safe state
remediationRetest: For any introduced fixture failure, correct the responsible retrieval, approval, effect, telemetry or evaluator boundary; retest the full legitimate and adverse flow before treating the change as release evidence.
recoveryTransfer: Perform one safe rollback/reconciliation after a policy/schema/build change, hand the setup to another reviewer for reproduction, then transfer the same security invariant to an unseen feature or second product surface.
limitations: Feature implementation is not yet built and the catalog’s 24 capstone cases are not yet run.
Onyx integration, actual-model behavior and external reviewer acceptance are not claimed.
The catalog’s starter recipe observations are preparation support only and are not attributed here as Ahmed’s independent results.
